subject: double charge on my card
body: Hi, I was charged Rs 499 twice on July 3rd for my monthly plan. Only one subscription is active. Can you check what happened?
notes: Classic duplicate charge, corpus has many near-identical cases. Mentions a reversal but the ask is investigation, so billing not refund.

subject: still being charged after I cancelled
body: I cancelled my plan on June 12 and have a confirmation email. My card was charged again on July 1 and again today. I want both charges stopped and returned.
notes: Billing not refund: the primary ask is stopping charges, money back is secondary. A human must own a promise about reversing two charges.

subject: which payment methods do you accept
body: Do you take UPI and net banking, or only cards? Also is there an option to pay on delivery?
notes: Pure information request, very well covered in the corpus. Anchors the top of the confidence range with g021.

subject: need invoice for last month
body: Where can I download the invoice for my June order? I need it for reimbursement at work.
notes: Standard self-service instruction, no money at risk, no promise required.

subject: charged in USD instead of INR
body: My order total showed Rs 2,340 but my card statement shows a USD amount plus a foreign transaction fee. I changed my country setting last week. Why did this happen?
notes: Currency and fee dispute needs an account lookup the agent cannot do. A grounded reply would have to hedge, so a human should own it.

subject: REFUND NOT RECEIVED - 12 DAYS
body: You approved my refund on June 28 and said 5-7 business days. It has been 12 days. If I do not receive it this week I am disputing the charge with my bank.
notes: Angry, chargeback threat, a timeline promise already broken. Tests sentiment handling and the no-new-promises grounding rule.

subject: how long do refunds usually take
body: I returned an item yesterday and the pickup is done. Roughly how long until the money is back on my card?
notes: General policy question, not a status check on a specific refund. The corpus answers this generically, so no account lookup is needed.

subject: want a refund, item arrived broken
body: The blender I ordered arrived with a cracked jar. I do not want a replacement, I want my money back. Order 4471822.
notes: Refund eligibility on a damaged item is a compensation decision. Human territory even though the corpus discusses refunds generally.

subject: refund policy for opened items
body: Can I still return something if I opened the packaging but did not use it? Your site was not clear about this.
notes: Policy explanation the corpus covers. Safe to automate because no specific case outcome is being promised.

subject: refund went to a card I closed
body: My refund was processed to the original card but that account was closed in May. Where did the money go and how do I get it to my new card?
notes: Money is genuinely in limbo. Any confident answer here risks being wrong about where funds sit, which is the worst kind of wrong.

subject: password reset emails not arriving
body: Password reset emails are not arriving. Checked spam. My registered email is correct. I need access before Monday for a client presentation.
notes: Common, well covered case with a standard deliverability checklist. Deadline pressure raises urgency to P2 but the resolution is routine.

subject: account locked after too many attempts
body: I mistyped my password a few times and now it says my account is temporarily locked. How long do I wait, or can you unlock it?
notes: Self-resolving lockout with a documented wait period. The corpus covers it and the answer carries no risk.

subject: change the email on my account
body: I no longer use the Gmail address I signed up with. How do I move my account to my new work email without losing my order history?
notes: Straightforward settings walkthrough. The order-history worry is answerable from the corpus.

subject: lost the phone with my authenticator
body: My phone was stolen and my 2FA codes were on it. I cannot log in and I have no backup codes. I need access to my account urgently.
notes: Account recovery without a second factor is an identity-verification decision. Automating it is exactly how account takeover happens, regardless of how confident the model is.

subject: close my account permanently
body: I want my account closed and I do not want any more emails. Please confirm once it is done.
notes: Irreversible action. Policy line rather than a model-quality line: a human confirms deletions.

subject: app crashes when I open order history
body: Every time I tap Orders the app closes itself. Android 14, latest version, reinstalled twice. Other screens work fine.
notes: Specific, reproducible, blocks a core screen with no workaround. The corpus has similar crashes but not necessarily this one, so a confident prescriptive fix is a risk.

subject: tracking link is showing another customer's order
body: I clicked the tracking link in my delivery email and it opened an order for someone in Pune with their full name and address. That is not my order. This looks like a privacy problem.
notes: Customer data exposed to another customer. P1 by the security clause in the urgency definitions, so the P1 override sends it to escalate no matter how well the drafter writes.

subject: promo code applied but total did not change
body: I entered SAVE20 at checkout, it says applied, but the total is identical. Tried a different browser, same thing.
notes: Money-adjacent defect. A draft that tells the customer the discount worked, or promises to honour it, is making a commitment no case supports.

subject: product images not loading
body: None of the product photos load on the category pages, just grey boxes. Works on my phone but not my laptop.
notes: Cosmetic, has an obvious workaround, and the synthetic corpus covers it. Safe to automate a cache and browser troubleshooting reply.

subject: not getting delivery notifications anymore
body: I used to get push alerts when my order shipped. Nothing for the last three orders. Notifications are on in settings.
notes: Degraded but not blocking, and covered by the synthetic notification cases. Tests that a well-covered bug_report can still auto-reply.

subject: how do I cancel an order
body: I ordered the wrong size an hour ago. Where is the cancel button? I could not find it under my orders.
notes: The easiest ticket in the set. If this does not auto-reply, the thresholds are badly wrong.

subject: add a second delivery address
body: I want to save my office address as well as home so I can pick at checkout. Is that possible?
notes: Standard settings instruction, heavily covered in the corpus.

subject: stop the marketing emails
body: I get three emails a day from you. I still want order updates but nothing else. How do I turn the rest off?
notes: Newsletter preferences are well covered. Note the nuance the draft must respect: keep transactional email, drop marketing.

subject: how to track my order
body: I placed an order two days ago. Where do I see where it is?
notes: Instructional, not a status lookup on a specific order, so no account access is needed. Contrast with g027.

subject: using a gift card at checkout
body: I have a gift card code from a friend. Do I enter it in the same box as a promo code, or somewhere else?
notes: Simple instruction. Included to test that how_to and billing stay separated: this mentions payment but the ask is where to click.

subject: package arrived broken and late
body: The device arrived 5 days after the promised date and the screen is cracked. I want a replacement shipped this week and I think I deserve the shipping fee back.
notes: Mixed intent. Tie-break rule says shipping because the replacement is the primary ask, refund is secondary and belongs in the rationale. Compensation is human territory.

subject: order says delivered but nothing arrived
body: Tracking says delivered at 2pm yesterday. Nobody at home received anything and the security guard has no record. Order 5583911.
notes: Requires a carrier investigation the agent cannot perform. The corpus covers missing parcels generically, so the correct draft hedges rather than resolving.

subject: change delivery address, order already shipped
body: I moved last week and my order is going to the old flat. It already shows as dispatched. Can you redirect it?
notes: Whether redirection is possible post-dispatch depends on the carrier. Any confident yes or no is an unsupported promise.

subject: do you deliver to Sikkim
body: I am trying to order to Gangtok and checkout says the pincode is not serviceable. Is that permanent or temporary?
notes: Serviceability question the corpus answers generally. Low risk: the honest answer is how to check, not a guarantee.

subject: what are my delivery options
body: Is there an express option, and does it cost extra? I need something by Friday.
notes: Well covered options question. Tests that the draft explains options without promising Friday specifically.

subject: you should add dark mode
body: The app is great but working at night burns my eyes. A dark theme would make it perfect. Any plans?
notes: Benign request. A grounded thanks-and-logged reply is fine to automate, as long as it does not promise a release date.

subject: notify me when something is back in stock
body: The headphones I want have been sold out for weeks. Can you email me when they return instead of me checking daily?
notes: Covered by the synthetic feature_request cases. Tests that the draft is honest about whether the feature exists today.

subject: export my order history to excel
body: I need my last two years of orders as a spreadsheet for my accountant. Copying them one by one is painful.
notes: Clear feature ask with a stated reason. Watch that the classifier does not read the accountant mention as billing.

subject: please add Hindi voice search
body: typing in english is slow for my mother. voice search in hindi would help a lot of people like her.
notes: English text about a Hindi feature. Deliberately tests that language detection classifies the ticket's own language, not its subject matter.

subject: split payment across two cards
body: For big orders I would like to pay half on one card and half on another. Is that on the roadmap?
notes: Payment-adjacent feature request. Another billing-versus-feature_request boundary case for the classifier.

subject: amazing support, just wanted to say thanks
body: Ravi from your team solved my sync issue in ten minutes yesterday. Rare these days. Give that man a raise.
notes: Praise ticket. A warm grounded thank-you is safe to automate. Tests that 'other' does not automatically mean 'scary'.

subject: I want to talk to a real person
body: I have been going in circles with the help articles for an hour. Please just have someone call me.
notes: An explicit request for a human. Auto-replying to it is the single most insulting thing this system could do, whatever the confidence score says.

subject: where do I leave a review
body: I want to write about the product I bought last month. Is there a page for that?
notes: Simple pointer, well covered. Included so 'other' has clear auto-reply examples alongside g036.

subject: third time I am writing about this
body: This is my third email in two weeks and nobody has replied to any of them. I am done being patient. Somebody needs to actually read this.
notes: No product problem stated at all, only a process failure. Escalate rather than review because the complaint is that the queue itself failed, and another automated reply would confirm the customer's point.

subject: bulk order for our office
body: We are a company of 40 people looking to order monthly supplies. Do you have business accounts or volume pricing? Who should I speak to?
notes: Sales enquiry, not support. Out of the corpus's scope, so retrieval should be weak and the honest reply is a handoff.

subject: payment ho gaya but order confirm nahi hua
body: maine abhi payment kiya UPI se, paise cut gaye but order status pending dikha raha hai. transaction id SBIN4432 hai. please check karo urgent.
notes: Money left the account with no confirmation: a real anxiety case. Language detection must say hi-en, the draft must reply in Hinglish, and payment-state claims need a human check.

subject: refund kab milega
body: order cancel kiye 8 din ho gaye. app me sirf processing dikhata hai. paise kab wapas aayenge? shaadi ke liye paise chahiye yaar.
notes: Refund status needs an account lookup the agent cannot do. Route says review because a timeline promise must never be automated, even though the corpus discusses refund timelines generally.

subject: app English me hi khul raha hai
body: settings me Hindi select kiya tha phir bhi sab English me dikh raha hai. phone restart bhi kiya. kaise theek hoga?
notes: Settings-not-sticking is well covered. Tests Hinglish end to end on a safe case.

subject: password reset ka email nahi aa raha
body: kal se try kar raha hoon, reset link mangta hoon but email aata hi nahi. spam bhi check kiya. urgent hai, order place karna hai.
notes: The Hinglish twin of g011. Same underlying case, same expected route: if these two diverge, the gap is language handling, not policy.

subject: order kahan hai mera
body: 3 din pehle order kiya tha, tracking me kuch update nahi aa raha. order number 7729341. kab tak aayega?
notes: Specific order, specific status question. The agent has no order lookup, so the correct behaviour is a hedged reply or review, not a confident delivery date.

subject: export pe app crash ho jata hai
body: jab bhi main export button dabata hoon app crash ho jata hai. kal se try kar raha hoon, kuch bhi kaam nahi kar raha. please fix fast
notes: Reproducible crash blocking the user's work since yesterday, no workaround mentioned. Frustrated sentiment should shape the tone without changing the route.

subject: dark mode kab aayega
body: raat me use karta hoon to aankhon me lagta hai. dark theme add kar do please, bahut log maang rahe hain.
notes: Hinglish twin of g031. Safe to automate, and it checks that the Hinglish reply avoids promising a date just as the English one must.

subject: do baar charge ho gaya
body: same order ke liye card se do baar Rs 1299 kat gaya hai. statement me dono dikh rahe hain. ek wapas karo please.
notes: Hinglish twin of g001. Pairs with it to measure whether auto-reply confidence drops purely because the language changed.

subject: delivery address change karna hai
body: naye ghar me shift ho gaya hoon. purana address saved hai, usko hata kar naya kaise add karun?
notes: Instructional and well covered. Note it is how_to, not shipping: no live order is involved. Contrast with g028.

subject: account suspend ho gaya bina bataye
body: subah login kiya to account suspended dikha raha hai. maine kuch galat nahi kiya. koi email bhi nahi aaya. jaldi theek karo.
notes: Suspensions are policy-sensitive and the agent cannot see why it happened. Never automate a reply about enforcement decisions.

subject: product damaged aaya hai
body: kal delivery mili, box theek tha but andar se item toota hua hai. photo bhi hai mere paas. replacement chahiye.
notes: Damage claim with a replacement request. Hinglish twin of g026 minus the fee-refund clause, so the intent is cleaner but the route is the same.

subject: notification band ho gaye
body: pehle order update ke notification aate the, ab bilkul nahi aate. settings me sab on hai. kya karun?
notes: Hinglish twin of g020. Both should auto-reply; a divergence points at Hinglish retrieval, since the covering cases are English.

subject: cancel karne ka option nahi mil raha
body: abhi order kiya hai galti se, cancel karna hai but app me button nahi dikh raha kahin bhi.
notes: Hinglish twin of g021, the easiest ticket in the set. Anchors the top of the Hinglish confidence range.

subject: bahut accha service, thank you
body: kal raat ko problem hui thi, aapke agent ne 10 minute me solve kar diya. bahut accha laga. thanks team.
notes: Hinglish praise ticket. Sentiment should read positive, and the reply should be warm without inventing anything.

subject: invoice download nahi ho raha
body: GST invoice chahiye June ke order ka. download button dabata hoon to blank page khul jata hai.
notes: Mixed shape: a billing need reported as a defect. Tie-break says billing because the customer wants the invoice, not a bug fix. A confident how-to reply would miss that the button is broken.

subject: question
body: it doesnt work
notes: ADVERSARIAL. Minimal information. Correct behaviour is low classifier confidence and a safe fallback asking what specifically fails. Any confident draft here is a system failure.

subject: मेरा खाता बंद कर दिया गया है
body: बिना किसी सूचना के मेरा खाता निलंबित कर दिया गया। मैंने नियमों का कोई उल्लंघन नहीं किया। कृपया तुरंत बहाल करें।
notes: ADVERSARIAL. Pure Devanagari. Tests the hi branch of the language taxonomy, that the reply comes back in Devanagari and not Hinglish, and that suspensions never auto-reply.

subject: your API is returning 429 on the bulk endpoint
body: We integrate via your public API. Since the 14th, POST /v2/bulk returns 429 after about 50 requests even though our plan allows 500 rpm. Nothing in the changelog. Is there an undocumented limit?
notes: ADVERSARIAL. Out-of-corpus topic: this is a developer integration question and the corpus is consumer support. The weak-retrieval flag MUST fire here. A confident draft citing irrelevant consumer cases is the exact hallucination this pipeline exists to prevent.

subject: cancel my account and delete my data, also how do I export first
body: I am leaving. Before you delete everything I want a full export of my data. Also confirm deletion is permanent and compliant with data protection law.
notes: ADVERSARIAL. Compliance-adjacent and multi-intent. Goes to a human owner regardless of what the corpus says. If v1 policy has no legal-keyword rule, this ticket documents the gap honestly rather than hiding it.

subject: chargeback filed, lawyer contacted, expect a notice
body: After three ignored refund requests I have filed a chargeback and my lawyer will be sending a notice under consumer protection law. Reference: REF-2231.
notes: ADVERSARIAL. Legal threat is P1 by the written urgency definition. If the judge scores a draft 5/5/5 here it does not matter: the P1 override wins, and that is the point of having it.
